key_insight: Continual learners in vision transformers perform best when task-specific adapters are placed in intermediate blocks, and a frozen brain-readout signal can identify those blocks without expensive placement search.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to cut adapter storage and tuning cost in lifelong learning while preserving accuracy, especially when deploying compact task-specific modules in ViT backbones.
method: Search all contiguous four-block adapter placements and compare accuracy across depths.
Use LS-B: a frozen fMRI encoding model over 12 human visual areas to rank blocks by task-varying readouts versus stable structure.
Select one fixed placement per backbone and evaluate under matched storage and observation budgets.
evidence_signal: Across three ViT-B/16 backbones, the chosen blocks align with intermediate-depth regions, and on Split ImageNet-R LS-B uses 60% of full-BiLoRA storage while staying within 1.5 pp of final accuracy.
watch_item: The allocation is backbone-specific and derived from fMRI-based readouts, so transferring the same placement rule to a new architecture or domain may require recalibration.
paper_title: Two Routes to the Middle: Placement Search and Brain Readouts Converge on Where Continual Learners Should Specialize
